The changed scheduleFiber path routes local workers externally when allWorkersBusy holds. rescheduleFiber above is unchanged, making benchmark call-path distinction essential.

Repeated cede dominates the benchmark loop, but initial traverse(...start) exists. The reviewer diagnosis is useful as a hot-path warning, not a literal assertion that the entire benchmark never calls start.

The unmerged optimization uses Arrays.copyOf for a packed Array[Int] stack. Any benchmark must model this element type, capacity growth and preserved count, not only large byte arrays or unrelated Object arrays.
Existing real-runtime regression starts concurrent queue work and waits for a completion counter to drain. It is a correctness/liveness probe, not a fairness or performance result.

Resource.make(IO(smallRuntime()))(rt => IO(rt.shutdown())).use { rt =>
        val io = for {
          p <- IO(Promise[Unit]())
          _ <- (IO.sleep(50.millis) *> IO(
            rt.scheduler.sleep(100.millis, () => p.success(())))).start
          _ <- IO(Await.result(p.future, Duration.Inf))
        } yield ()

        List
          .fill(10)(io.start)
          .sequence
          .flatMap(_.traverse(_.joinWithNever))
          .evalOn(rt.compute) >> IO(ok)
      }
evidence.interpretation: Existing real-runtime regression owns a small runtime, injects delayed work and joins started fibers before release. A historical class name does not establish which current scheduler mechanism is exercised.

claims.rule: For a scheduler optimization, trace the benchmark into schedule versus reschedule, record callback origin, and measure the intended fairness or throughput metric. Internal Queue traffic must not stand in for external IO without proving the same placement path.
claims.applicability: Observed review practice in CE3 JVM WorkStealingThreadPool history; use fresh version-specific call-graph and profiling evidence before applying to another runtime. Report authored benchmark results separately from measurements actually reproduced.
claims.counterexample: A cede-heavy loop still has an initial start phase but is weak evidence about steady-state initial placement. An optimization that helps a synthetic internal priority pattern does not prove improved fairness for external NIO callbacks.

claims.rule: Require the actual element type, growth regime, platform and end-to-end bottleneck to match before treating a JVM intrinsic substitution as a runtime improvement; retain semantic and platform tests even if a microbenchmark is favorable.
claims.applicability: Inference from rejected 2021-2024 runtime optimizations. Arrays.copyOf may be suitable elsewhere; this history only rejects an unsupported benefit claim for these paths. No current benchmark or Native execution has been performed.
claims.counterexample: Large-byte-array SIMD results do not directly characterize ByteStack, whose packed representation is Array[Int], or establish that stack growth is limiting real IO throughput.
